subject: DI03000091

body.en:
Understand the idea

Anull-comparison instrument measures an unknown DCemfagainst a calibrated adjustable voltage without drawing current from the unknown at balance.

Explanation and application

  • Construction:a stable DCworking supply,rheostat,calibrated resistance wire/dials,standard reference,selector/null detector and opposing-polarity test connection.
  • Standardise first:adjust working current until the standard emfbalances its stated dial/length setting;this establishes voltage per division.Keep reference temperature/loading limits.
  • Select the unknown with correct polarity and vary calibrated setting until detector current is zero;read unknown emfonly at null.Change of working supply requires restandardisation.
  • Applications:emfcomparison,cell internal resistance under an approved load method,and calibration via known shunts/dividers.The potentiometer does not safely accept arbitrary mains voltage.
Why potentiometer null?

At balance no current is drawn from the unknown branch.

body.en:
Given and assumptions

Uniform wire,constant working current;standard Esbalances at lsand unknown Exat lx.

Step-by-step solution

  1. The calibrated potential gradient k=Es/ls(volts per unit length).
  2. At null,the unknown branch current is zero,so Exequals the selected wire drop:Ex=k lx.
  3. Substitute k:Ex=Es(lx/ls).For Es1.018V,ls50cm,lx30cm,Ex0.6108V.

Interpretation and check

Nonuniform wire,changed working current or detector loading away from null invalidates a casual length-ratio reading.

Understand the idea

Calibrated resistance selections replace a long single sliding wire;coarse and fine settings cover the selected range.

Explanation and application

  • The main/coarse dial selects larger known resistance increments;the second/fine dial interpolates smaller increments at the same standardised working current.
  • Standard cell/reference and working-current controls establish calibration;the null detector compares the sum of selected drops with the unknown.
  • Read Ex=coarse contribution+fine contribution under the actual range/multiplier setting.Check the instrument manual rather than inventing a universal dial graduation.
  • Illustrative declared dials:0.1Vper coarse step and0.001Vper fine step;settings7and25give0.725V.These values illustrate reading,not an official Crompton specification.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Select the method by lead/contact error,loading and leakage,not merely a memorised numerical boundary.

Explanation and application

  • Low resistance often means below about1Ωin textbook classification;lead/contact drops become significant,so four-terminal/Kelvin techniques are preferred.
  • Medium is commonly about1Ωto100kΩand high above about100kΩ;boundaries vary by text/instrument.High-Rmeasurement requires leakage control,guarding and adequate settling.
  • Insulation resistance depends strongly on test voltage,time,temperature and moisture;record them with the result.Never choose the highest tester voltage just to get a reading.

body.en:
Given and assumptions

Diamond A–B–C–D:RxonAB,RsonBC,RponAD,RqonDC;source A–C,detector B–D.

Step-by-step solution

  1. At null VB=VDand detector current is zero;each source branch then behaves as an independent potential divider.
  2. Taking Czero and source VAC,V B=VAC Rs/(Rx+Rs);V D=VAC Rq/(Rp+Rq).
  3. Equating and cross-multiplying gives RsRp=RqRx.Hence Rx=RsRp/Rq.
  4. Example:Rs100Ω,Rp200Ω,Rq50Ωgives Rx400Ω.Balance sensitivity and lead resistance limit useful accuracy.

Interpretation and check

Resistor ratios and detector/source placement must match the stated topology;reversing a labelled arm changes the formula.

ક્રમબદ્ધ ઉકેલ

  1. NullપરVB=VD/detectorIzeroછે.બંનેbranchesindependentpotentialdividersબને.
  2. CzeroલેતાંVB=VAC Rs/(Rx+Rs)/VD=VAC Rq/(Rp+Rq)છે.
  3. Equate/cross-multiplyકરતાંRsRp=RqRxછે.તેથીRx=RsRp/Rqછે.
  4. ExampleRs100Ω,Rp200Ω/Rq50ΩથીRx400Ωછે.Balancesensitivity/leadRaccuracyનેમર્યાદિતકરે.

અર્થ અને ચકાસણી

Understand the idea

It measures very low resistance using separate current/potential connections and a second ratio pair.

Explanation and application

  • Construction:unknown Rx,standard S,main ratio P/Q,auxiliary ratio p/q,low-resistance connecting link r,controlled source and null detector.
  • Potential leads sample the resistor terminals without carrying the main test current;the auxiliary divider compensates the link-voltage contribution when ratios match.
  • For the declared Kelvin topology,Rx=(P/Q)S+[rq/(p+q+r)](P/Q−p/q).When P/Q=p/q,the link-error term vanishes and Rx=(P/Q)S.
  • Use stable limited current,good contacts and appropriate polarity reversal/thermal-emfcontrol for the trainer.Two-wire low-ohm readings cannot simply be called Kelvin measurements.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Acontrolled high-DCvoltage insulation tester infers high resistance from applied voltage and leakage current.

Explanation and application

  • Classical construction includes a DCgenerator/source,deflecting/control coils or ratio mechanism,range circuit and test terminals;modern units use electronic measurement and regulated test voltage.
  • Isolate the equipment,verify dead,disconnect sensitive electronics as authorised and select the manufacturer-approved test voltage/time;high tester ranges are capabilities,not required student settings.
  • R≈Vtest/Ileakunder stable conditions;charging/absorption current means the indicated resistance may change with time.Guard terminals can exclude specified surface leakage paths.
  • After testing,allow the approved discharge and verify safe residual voltage before touch/reconnection.Insulation test pass/fail comes from the applicable equipment standard,not an invented universal MΩlimit.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Measure electrode-to-earth resistance with a controlled test current and separate potential measurement.

Explanation and application

  • The approved three-terminal arrangement uses electrode E,potential probe Pand current probe C;the tester drives current between E/Cand measures voltage E/P.
  • R≈VEP/IECwhen probe fields and conditions suit the method;move the potential probe through several positions to check a stable region rather than trust one convenient reading.
  • The familiar62%position is conditional on adequate separation and suitable soil/electrode geometry,not a universal shortcut.
  • Electrode disconnection can remove protective earthing:only authorised personnel may plan it with alternate protection.Never defeat a building earth for a student test.

body.en:
Given and assumptions

Use impedances Z1AB,Z2BC,Z3AD,Z4DC;source A–C,detector B–D.

Step-by-step solution

  1. At null VB=VD;the complex potential-divider relation is Z2/(Z1+Z2)=Z4/(Z3+Z4).
  2. Cross-multiplication gives Z1Z4=Z2Z3,or Z1/Z2=Z3/Z4.
  3. Both real and imaginary parts must balance;two independent adjustments are generally required.Standard capacitors/resistors and suitable ACnull detectors provide references.

Interpretation and check

Choose a bridge for R,L,Cor frequency;Wien-type arrangements can measure frequency,but a component bridge is not automatically frequency-independent.

ક્રમબદ્ધ ઉકેલ

  1. NullપરVB=VDછે.ComplexdividerrelationZ2/(Z1+Z2)=Z4/(Z3+Z4)છે.
  2. Cross-multiplyથીZ1Z4=Z2Z3અથવાZ1/Z2=Z3/Z4મળે.
  3. Real/imaginaryબંનેbalanceજોઈએ.સામાન્યરીતેબેindependentadjustmentsજોઈએ.StandardC-R/ACnulldetectorreferencesઆપે.

અર્થ અને ચકાસણી

Given and assumptions

Z1=1/(jωCx),Z2=R2,Z3=1/(jωCs),Z4=R4;Csis the known capacitor.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Use Z1Z4=Z2Z3:R4/(jωCx)=R2/(jωCs).
  2. Cancel the common jωfactor: R4/Cx=R2/Cs,so Cx=CsR4/R2.
  3. Example:Cs0.1µF,R4=200Ω,R2=100Ω gives Cx0.2µF.
  4. This simple bridge assumes low-loss capacitors;unequal dielectric losses prevent a true null with resistance-ratio adjustment alone.It does not independently measure loss angle.

Interpretation and check

Arm labels are essential;swapping capacitor/resistor positions can invert the apparent ratio.

Connections and instruments

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. Identify ratings,ranges,terminals,test conditions and stop criteria;prepare an approved diagram and reference/uncertainty plan.

Poor null may arise from contact resistance,wrong arms,battery or detector sensitivity;rewire only dead.
